full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff filed the suit for permanent injunction restraining defendant No.1 from disturbing the plaintiffs' peaceful possession in the suit land. The plaint case is that the suit jote appertaining to CS Khatian No.377 of Rasulpur Mouja belong to defendant Nos.1-2 as chaua rayat at a rental of 9 maunds 18 seers and 12 chataks paddy under Sharat Shundari Devi. Defendants Asiruddin Mondal and Easin Ali Mondal possessed the suit jote in equal share and the CS khgtian was prepared in their names accordingly. During the revisional rent roll operation the suit jote was also recorded in the names of the defendants and the paddy rent has been commuted into money rent of Rs.3/55 and they paid rents of the jote to the Government. Defendant No. 1 transferred more than 10 bighas of land in violation of Ordinance No. XXXIII of 1951 For this offence defendant No. 1 was fined as he did not pay the fine in time. A Certificate Case No. 6 AM/59-60 was started in the Bogra Certificate Court and after due service of the processes and observance of the relevant provisions of law the suit land and other lands of defendant No. 1 was auction sold to the plaintiffs on 10-8-62 after due publicity and within the knowledge of defendant No. 1. The sale was confirmed on 15-10- 62. The plaintiff got the sale certificate and took the delivery of possession of the auction purchased land on 8-12-62 by beat of drum and since then they have been possessing the land by personal cultivation, After taking delivery of possession the plaintiff by amicable partition with proforma defendant No. 2 got the suit land and have been in exclusive possession of the same. Defendant No. 1 no interest and possession in the suit land. But defendant No. 1 has recently created some dakhilas in the name of his wife and in collusion with the settlement employee caused the MR Khatian of the suit land to be prepared in the name of his wife. The story of pattan of the suit land in the name of his wife is fictitious and the plaintiff got the MR Khatian corrected in their names on application under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act to the Revenue Officer on 24-12-66. At this defendant No.1 became very enraged and on 8- 3-67 defendant No.1 came to the suit land to resist the plaintiff and his laborers to plough the land and the plaintiff drove away defendant No. 1. But while leaving the spot he threatened that he will possess the suit land by any means. These activities on the part of defendant No. 1 have caused breach of peace and irreparable loss to the plaintiff. Hence the suit. 

 8. The learned Single Judge found that in the written statement defendant No. 1 clearly stated that he took pattan of 0.58 acres of suit land from Ex. Rent Receiver in the name of his wife as back as in 1355 BS by Exts. A-2. The learned Single Judge believed the rent receipts of Pasiran and paying of rents to the Ex Rent Receiver and thereafter to the Government. The learned Single Judge considered the exhibits namely, the dakhilas and the MR Khatian and found clear prima facie title of Pasiran Bibi. The learned Single Judge also found that Pasiran transferred her 0.58 acres of land to her two daughters by registered Kabala. The learned Single Judge found that the last court of fact has not given due consideration to the oral and documentary evidences on record as has been produced by the defendant and wrongly reversed the findings of the trial Court. The learned Single Judge also found that the lower appellate Court unreasonably placed more reliance on the material oral evidence of the plaintiff's witnesses and disbelieved the deposition of defendants' witness without giving any valid and cogent reasons. The learned Single Judge also found that the finding of the lower appellate Court with regard to question of partial surrender is also not legally tenable. The learned Single Judge found that the lower appellate Court wrongly found that defendant No. 1 alone surrendered the suit land without the consent of his co-sharer brother defendant No. 2. It is on record that by amicable arrangements defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were possessing separately and, as such, defendant No.2 was not a party to the alleged surrender and consent of defendant No.2 as co-sharer was not at all necessary as per section 86(7) of Bengal Tenancy Act. This material aspect was lost sight of by the lower appellate Court which wrongly found fault with defendant No. 2 for not appearing to depose in the case. Thus, the reasons given by the lower appellate Court for non-appearance of defendant No. 2 was wrong as found by the learned Single Judge. In such circumstances, the learned Single Judge on due consideration of the oral and documentary evidences on record found that the finding of fact arrived at by the lower appellate Court is based on misreading and non-consideration of the material evidence on record and consequently interfered with the findings of fact arrived at by the lower appellate Court.
